key_insight: Lipid-based AI models linked lower LDL cholesterol to subsequent heart failure, highlighting a counterintuitive association rather than a causal effect.
clinical_relevance: Routine lipid panels supplemented with ApoB may offer signals for heart failure risk research, but clinical usefulness remains unestablished.
method: Analyzed age-matched, multicenter All of Us electronic health records retrospectively.
Used machine learning to predict first heart failure diagnosis within 36 months and distinguish cases from people never diagnosed with cardiovascular disease.
Applied SHAP to interpret lipid contributions, with sex-specific analyses.
evidence_signal: Reported AUCs were 0.624 for men and 0.627 for women for 36-month prediction, versus 0.937 and 0.925 when comparing heart failure cases with cardiovascular-disease-free controls.
watch_item: The large performance difference across comparison groups cautions against treating case-control discrimination as evidence of reliable prospective screening.
paper_title: Cholesterol Paradox: Multi-point Heart Failure Prediction from Lipid Panels in Electronic Health Records
